  (two machines, independent builds). Raw formulations of the same case need
  600-850 GB — explains why this sat unresolved since 2022.
- Line probe (validated on solved case): open subcase (2) has NO codim-1
  solution family at p ∈ {65521, 1048573, 2147483629}. Remaining outcomes:
  empty-with-deep-certificate, or small deep solution locus (= candidate
  counterexample towers).
- Verdict pending: msolve on the open cores (fleet: ultramem-1 + jc-b).
  Spot preemptions are the operational enemy; ~20h jobs lost twice.

### Standing ops rules (consolidated 2026-08-19; the loop reads these, not its prompt)
- Roles: Fable coordinates+researches; Sol equal co-researcher; Grok hostile
  reviewer. Dual review before promotion; honest reporting; NOTHING external
  without DC. Citation = merit only. CAS batch-mode only.
- Fleet: AWS only; no local msolve; solver jobs orphan-safe with completion
  echoes AND launch markers AND -v2 telemetry; verify launches/deaths by
  SPECIFIC-pattern process count (never head-truncate, second probe before
  any death diagnosis).
- Kills: inspect PIDs first; kill literal PIDs only; the target pattern may
  appear NOWHERE else in the same remote command (echo-log separately);
  never pkill-then-relaunch in one command.
- Memory: shed order = unrelated lanes -> telemetry-condemned lanes -> the
  sacrificial prime lane (p200257 first: no rational chart points); protect
  2 primes minimum (EMPTY 2+ tree).
- Decisive-object defaults: 48h caps; race reduced vs full presentations
  when a build is cheap; both finishing = integrity cross-check.

### Ideation cadence (DC ratified 2026-08-19): event-triggered + daily floor
Fresh ideation rounds (Fable + Sol INDEPENDENT lists: software accelerations
+ new math avenues) fire on EVENTS, not a fixed clock:
  (a) a decisive lane verdicts or caps/timeouts (postmortem = ideation);
  (b) a new object is banked (GB, census, theorem, reduced form);
  (c) an external actor moves (sweep hit);
  (d) FLOOR: 12h elapsed with none of the above (DC tightened from 24h, 2026-08-21).
Rationale: idea yield tracks STATE CHANGES, not elapsed time; a fixed 6h
timer re-rolls the same dice on unchanged state (overlap, token cost,
review debt) while still lagging real events by up to 6h. Event triggers
beat any fixed cadence on both latency and cost. External world-sweep
stays DAILY (the world changes on its own clock). Grok laterals join the
event rounds as the third independent list when the event is mathematical.

### Software doctrine (DC, 2026-08-18): first-class citizen
Software upgrades are a FIRST-CLASS CITIZEN of the campaign, not a daily
afterthought. Default posture: aggressive parallelization + acceleration.
Concretely: (a) when a computation is projected > ~2h, ALWAYS ask whether an
engine-level reduction (FLINT pre-elimination, structure exploitation,
better emission) could preempt it, and if plausible BUILD AND RACE it in
parallel on spare fleet RAM rather than waiting; (b) racing reduced systems
against full systems doubles as an integrity cross-check when both finish;
(c) every tool ships with gates and an INTERNAL/UNREVIEWED label until it
feeds a promoted claim, then it enters the review gauntlet like any math.

## 2026-08-23 msolve SIGSEGV: PR opened (32-bit exponent-index overflow)
- Root cause: not F4 hash growth. Parser `store_exponent` takes
  `(pos+j)*nvars` as int32_t; SIGSEGV once `nterms*nvars > INT32_MAX`.
  gdb: `pos=-2147477296` at iofiles.c:58. Bracket: upto38 (10.5M terms,
  172 vars, product 1.81e9) computes; upto40 (18.9M terms, product 3.26e9)
  faults; full 1.05 GB file also wraps the uint32 calloc.
- Fix: 64-bit offsets/allocs in iofiles.c + set_exponent_vector + var-order
  swap. Minimized reproducer (10000 vars, 214750 copies of x0, ~700KB):
  unpatched SIGSEGV, patched computes GB. `make check` 64/64.
- PR: https://github.com/algebraic-solving/msolve/pull/355
  (`dcposch:fix-int32-exp-overflow`, Co-Authored-By: Grok via the JC2 campaign).
  Details in ops/msolve-issue-draft.md.

## EVENT ~16:58Z — EXACT-N PROPOSAL: THE BOTTOM OF MOH'S TREE IS RIGID (flagship `exact-n-rigidity-opus5-20260902` launched, hostile)

From Grok's round submission (§4, the "Wronskian dictionary"): along a
root τ_i of g − c₂, d/dx f(x,τ_i) = ±1/g_y(τ_i) and g_y(τ_i) =
∏_{j≠i}(τ_i − τ_j) (monic), so with the shifted-tree structure of
FRONTIER-N, ord_t g_y(τ_i) = −δ⁰_i and the pole of f along τ_i is
EXACTLY 1 − δ⁰_i (δ⁰_i = g-frontier level of ρ_i; δ⁰_i = 1 impossible):
N = Σ_i (1 − δ⁰_i)⁺, a function of the unshifted g-tree alone (DICT-N).
Coordinator's squeeze: (frontier definition) δ⁰_i ≤ δ₁ − λ_g(δ₁), so
pole_i ≥ 1 − δ₁ + λ_g(δ₁) = d(1−δ₁)/(d+e) by RADIUS-ORDER at r = 1;
(FRONTIER-N + monotonicity + major-tower proportionality) pole_i ≤
−λ_f(δ₁) = d(1−δ₁)/(d+e). EQUALITY ⇒ the sub-tree of every bottom-major
disc is a STAR (all a₁ + b₁ roots separate exactly at δ₁), every
bottom-major root has pole d(1−δ₁)/(d+e), and
   N = A_bot · d(1−δ₁)/(d+e)   (EXACT-N; A_bot = # g-roots in
   bottom-major discs ≤ ue; N = U iff the cover is exact).
Consequences if it survives review: OPEN[D1-SUBTREE] closed by rigidity;
the filter is exact and two-sided (N ∈ Z ∩ [6,16]); Moh's survivor with
U = 10.5 dies; degrees may EMPTY. The r = 1 identity that makes the
squeeze tight, (1−δ₁) + λ_g(δ₁) = −λ_f(δ₁), was found by Grok (§4.3,
"a coincidence that is not a floor") — the lane is charged to decide
whether it is Moh's definition of δ₁ in disguise. Deeper g–g contact
RAISES N (the f-tree is slaved), inverting the N-ON-THE-TREE lane's
"free sub-tree can only lower N". Status: PROPOSAL; hostile lane out.

Math. Vietnam32(2007),243--246,

Section4 starts from f=y^2+B(x)y+x/4, B=x^2+x-1/2. Its degree27 f4 is obtained
by composing these birational source substitutions, in the printed order:
(X,y)->(X+y,y); (v,w)->(1/v,-v/4+v^2w);
(V,w)->(-(V+1-(512/45)w)*36/5,w);
(x,y)->(1/x,-5x/144+x^2y). Their determinants are1,-1,-36/5,-1,
so the composite determinant is -36/5. The paper's nonsingularity,
irreducibility and boundary assertions are source assertions, not independently
reconstructed here; none is needed for the following obstruction.

ROOT manual argument, UNREVIEWED: over K=C(t), the generic fibre f=t has
w=2y+B(x) and w^2=Delta_t(x)=x^4+2x^3-2x+1/4+4t. Its derivative is
2(x+1)^2(2x-1), with Delta_t(-1)=5/4+4t and Delta_t(1/2)=-7/16+4t,
so the quartic is squarefree over K. On its smooth projective genus-one
completion, dx/w is nonzero and regular everywhere: at a finite branch point
x-a has order2 and w order1; at either infinity, x has pole1 and w pole2.
If rational q satisfied J(f,q)=c in C*, restriction to the generic fibre
would give dq=-c dx/w. In characteristic zero a pole of a rational function
forces a pole of its differential; thus q would have no poles on the proper
curve and dq=0, a contradiction. A constant-J birational source substitution
transports any rational mate back by its rational inverse and the chain rule.
Consequently this literal f4 has no rational mate, without expanding f4 or
bounding the degree of a prospective mate. No conclusion about other degree27
polynomials, arbitrary birational transformations, or actual Keller pairs.

  1=(1+6xy^2)(1-6xy^2)+(2y^3)(18x^2y).

For z=ty^2, a=(1-4z)^(1/2) with a(0)=1, and A=a^3, its formal flow is

  y_t=y/a,
  x_t=x A + [A-(1-4z)]/(2y^2).

Indeed P(x_t,y_t)=P(x,y), dy_t/dt=2y_t^3, and the initial values agree.
All coefficients lie in Z[x,y]: a^(-1) has central-binomial coefficients,
a=1-2 sum_{n>=1} Catalan_{n-1} z^n, and
A-(1-4z)=(1-4z)(a-1) belongs to 2z Z[[z]]. Formal-flow uniqueness over Q
gives iterativity, which descends to the integral coefficients. Thus the
coefficient operators E_n satisfy D^n=n! E_n, and D^p=0 modulo EVERY prime.

y_t^2=y^2/(1-4ty^2) has an odd-order pole in t and is not a square there.

would make f(1+2x) polynomial, hence f polynomial. Its addition cannot
remove the remaining y=0 pole. The rational slice is not a polynomial
mate; this is NOT a Keller counterexample or a full-frame countercontrol.

## 2026-09-13 18:21 UTC — full-pair radial indices: boundary cancellation

NO_MATHEMATICAL_ADVANCE / NO_CLOSING_TEST, MANUAL/UNPROMOTED. ROOT
revalidated the preceding arithmetic-flow NO_PROGRESS against fresh pins
and LIVE state. The selected test uses an ACTUAL full polynomial Keller
pair, not another vector-field control: can global radial/pencil indices
force geometric degree N=1? The checked identities do not.

Translate a generic target point to the origin. The polynomial field V
defined by V(P)=P, V(Q)=Q has divergence2 and exactly N affine zeros, each
with linearization I. For its saturated projective foliation of degree d,

  4N + BB_infinity = (d+2)^2,
   N + Milnor_infinity = d^2+d+1.

The second gives only a degree-dependent bound. The first retains an
uncontrolled boundary sum: dx wedge dy becomes meromorphic, and boundary
foliation generators must be rescaled, so their traces need not be2.
For a generic invariant pencil curve C of degree e, CS_affine=N and
CS_total=e^2, matching Bezout's N+intersection_infinity=e^2. Blowing up
an affine radial zero makes its exceptional curve TRANSVERSE, not invariant;
there is no Camacho--Sad constraint for that curve as an invariant divisor.

ROOT's explicit boundary correction removes a possible misleading shortcut.
Suppose m=deg P<n=deg Q, k=n-m; let p,q be their degree-m/n homogenizations,
z the infinity coordinate, and f=z^k p, g=q. Then

  f dg-g df = z^(k-1) Omega,
  Omega = z(p dq-q dp)-k p q dz.

Omega is the saturated homogeneous form: it has no affine common factor
(affine zeros are isolated), and z does not divide its dz coefficient.
Its coefficient degree is m+n, so d=m+n-1. For a generic reduced member
h=f-lambda*g, lambda!=0,infinity, the exact identity is

  z^(k-1) Omega = -g dh+h dg.

The GSV definition therefore gives branch order ord(g)-(k-1)ord(z) on
the normalization of h=0. Summing at infinity, with all multiplicities,

  GSV_infinity = I_infinity(h,g)-(k-1)I_infinity(h,z)
               = (n^2-N)-(k-1)n = n(m+1)-N.

Adding the affine N gives n(m+1), exactly (d+2)n-n^2. N cancels. This
retains singularities of h at infinity and is not a smooth-boundary or
reduced-intersection assumption. It yields no new inequality or degree bound.

For k>=2 the RAW form has a divisorial zero; its pair Milnor number at
infinity basepoints is infinite, unlike the finite intersection multiplicity
of the FUNCTION ideal (f,g). Saturation changes the former and leaves the
nonreduced pencil member z^k p present. Changing generators of this same
pencil does not remove that member. Thus affine smoothness cannot be used
to assert that the full projective pencil has only reduced members.

**Global coordinate slices: MANUAL/UNPROMOTED degree preservation.**
Let Phi=(p,q,r):A3_C->A3_C have J(p,q,r)=1 and generic degree d.
Set k=C(p,q), K=C(x,y,z), D(a)=J(p,q,a), M=ker(D|K).
For ANY a in M, differentiate its monic minimal polynomial over k(r).
The differentiated polynomial has smaller degree and vanishes at a, so
its coefficients vanish: all original coefficients belong to k. Thus M/k
is algebraic. Each finite subextension has degree<=d, since r is
transcendental and K/k(r) has degree d; hence M/k is finite.
If a polynomial H satisfies D(H)=1 GLOBALLY, H-r belongs to M and

  M(H)=M(r),
  [K:k(H)]=[K:M(H)]*[M:k]=[K:k(r)]=d.

If H is moreover a SOURCE POLYNOMIAL COORDINATE, complete it to (U,V,H)
with Jacobian lambda in C*. Chain rule gives J_(U,V)(p,q)=1/lambda on
EVERY plane H=c. Every fibre of Phi_H=(p,q,H) has <=d points: any d+1
distinct points would persist under local inverse branches on a common
analytic target neighborhood meeting the generic degree-d locus.
Therefore every plane restriction is Keller with mapping degree<=d.
For d<=5 the accepted external plane low-sheet theorem makes every such
restriction an automorphism; consequently Phi_H has singleton fibres and
d=1. No noninvertible degree2--5 Keller triple admits this global slice.

ROOT's MANUAL/UNPROMOTED discriminator distinguishes that quadric from T,
independently of any missing Peretz theorem. After t=2Y+1,z=4Z,x=X, the
quadric is Q={xz=t^2-1}, whereas T={x^2z=t^2-1}. Their global residue forms
are eta_Q=dx wedge dt/x and eta_T=dx wedge dt/x^2. At x=0,t=+/-1 each
extends as dx wedge dz/(2t), so both are everywhere nonvanishing.
On Q the real sphere x=a+ib,z=-a+ib,t=c,a^2+b^2+c^2=1 has
eta_Q=i dphi wedge dc off its poles, hence integral +/-4*pi*i !=0.
Thus eta_Q is NOT exact. On T,

  eta_T=d lambda,
  lambda=-t*z dx-(t*x/2)dz+x*z dt = -dt/x on x!=0.

The displayed polynomial one-form extends globally; the relation verifies
the equality and exactness on the dense chart, hence everywhere. Q has
only constant regular units: localization at x is C[x,x^-1,t], so a unit
must be c*x^m; vanishing orders on either x=0 line force m=0. Therefore
any hypothetical regular etale Q->T would pull eta_T to c*eta_Q for c!=0,
contradicting the period. In particular the two surfaces are not regularly
isomorphic, and an etale Q->T cannot transfer Q's obstruction. This stops
that specific resemblance/transfer shortcut, NOT every possible theorem
on T and NOT a regular pair on T/S. No novelty claim, FIRST/promotion,
general-surface control, gauge or higher-exponent successor is selected.

**Finite disjointness observation.** Let C=V(h) be an irreducible affine
plane curve over C which is not isomorphic to A1, with h irreducible.
Only finitely many irreducible closed curves D with normalization A1 can
be disjoint from C. Indeed, for a normalization gamma:A1->D, h(gamma(t))
has no zero and therefore is a nonzero constant c. Thus D is a component
of h=c. Outside finitely many values c, h-c is irreducible and its zero
set is smooth. Such a D would be the entire smooth fibre, hence A1.
Abhyankar-Moh-Suzuki straightens D to a coordinate line. Since h-c is
irreducible, it is a nonzero scalar times that coordinate, making h itself
a coordinate up to affine change; then C is A1, a contradiction. All
possible D therefore lie in finitely many exceptional fibres, each with
finitely many components.

Exact external inputs checked, not reproved: Bodin, arXivmath/0510434v3,
https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0510434v3 , Corollary2.4, printed3: apply with
p=h and q=1 to obtain irreducibility of h-c outside finitely many c.
This avoids assuming a connected-fibre conclusion from an arbitrary
irreducible special fibre without justification. Smoothness fails only
at finitely many critical values: the critical locus has finitely many
components and h is constant on each positive-dimensional one in
characteristic0. Palka, arXiv1405.5391v2,
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1405.5391v2 , TheoremB, printed1, states the exact
embedded-A1 straightening used here. Only the indicated theorem contexts
were checked; no whole-paper proof audit or new foundational promotion.

framework, but is unnecessary to this proof. Incidental secondary/social

## 2026-09-14 03:26 UTC — affine rational singularities; the infinity gap survives

MANUAL/UNPROMOTED, KNOWN compactification theorem with an actual-source
attachment. Previous turn made navigation progress but no mathematics.
This bounded pass identifies a valid structural restriction, not a global
closing implication or a new theorem of compactification theory.

Let F=(f,g) be a nonlinear complex plane Keller map, rho:Y->P2_target its
FULL-field finite projective normalization, and pi:Z->P2_source,
sigma:Z->Y a common resolution extending the source open immersion.
Write L for the strict original source infinity line, D=max(deg f,deg g)>1.
On generic L the map to target infinity is constant: for unequal degrees
this is immediate; for equal degrees the Keller identity gives
J(f_D,g_D)=0, and equal-degree binary homogeneous forms are proportional.
Finiteness of rho therefore gives sigma(L)={q}, with rho(q) at infinity.

Every sigma-contracted curve lies in the source boundary, since any curve
meeting A2 would contradict quasi-finiteness of F. Outside sigma^-1(q),
all such curves are pi-exceptional. Connected sigma-fibers make pi constant
on each whole fiber. The reduced image of (sigma,pi) in
(Y\{q}) x P2_source projects properly, quasi-finitely and birationally to
normal Y\{q}; it is therefore the graph of a descended birational morphism.
The descended morphism need NOT itself be proper.

The exact general result is already in Pinaki Mondal,
https://pinakimondal.org/papers/compact-general-v16.pdf , Theorem1.1(2).
Its proof on printed18 identifies the sole possible nonsandwiched point
as the contraction of the original infinity line. The auxiliary
compactification in that proof dominates the smooth source plane and
agrees with Y away from q, supplying the proper LOCAL sandwich. Footnote2,
printed2, cites sandwiched=>rational. Consequently every singularity of
Y away from q is rational, in particular EVERY singularity of the affine
finite normalization. This does not assert that q is singular/nonrational,
that all projective singularities are rational, or that the pair (Y,R/2)
is numerically log canonical anywhere. Rationality is not a bound on R.

## 2026-09-14 03:54 UTC — polynomial inverse need not terminate in raw depth

Previous goal turn: PROGRESS as a bounded negative selection test, not a
new actual-source constraint or JC2 theorem. This turn leaves the boundary
control line and tests an all-degree inverse proposal directly: does
polynomial invertibility force eventual vanishing of the raw-depth terms
in the Abhyankar--Gurjar formula? NO, even for a two-shear automorphism.
MANUAL/PRODUCER-CHECKED with same-model co-research; UNPROMOTED.

Let z=(x,y), and write

    F=(x+y^2, y+(x+y^2)^2),
    H=z-F=(-y^2,-(x+y^2)^2),
    G=(x-(y-x^2)^2, y-x^2).

Direct composition gives F G=G F=id, and JF=1. In Zhao0907.3991v2,
Theorem3.1, the literal depth-m term for a polynomial q is

    A_m(q)=sum_(a+b=m) partial_x^a partial_y^b(q H1^a H2^b)/(a!b!),
    q(G)=sum_(m>=0) A_m(q).

For q=y, expand y H1^a H2^b as
(-1)^(a+b) sum_(j=0..2b) binom(2b,j) x^j y^(2a+4b-2j+1).
A nonzero differentiated term requires j>=a and has total degree
1+a+3b-j <= 1+3m-3a. The unique term of degree3m+1 has a=j=0,b=m.
Consequently, for EVERY m>=1,

    deg A_m(y)=3m+1,
    [y^(3m+1)] A_m(y)=(-1)^m (4m+1)!/(m!(3m+1)!) != 0.

Every finite cutoff through M>=1 retains this top term from A_M, whereas
G2=y-x^2 has degree2; M=0 also fails. NO finite raw-depth truncation works
on this example. The infinite sum is nevertheless well-defined formally,
since each term has order at least m+1. Polynomiality results from
cancellation across depths, not termination before summation.

The exact regrouping shows what cancels. For each fixed b, sum over a
first, before the outer y derivatives. Since H1=-y^2 is x-independent,
the finite Taylor shift x->x-y^2 sends y(x+y^2)^(2b) to y*x^(2b).
Thus the double series becomes

    sum_(b>=0) (-1)^b partial_y^b(y*x^(2b))/b! = y-x^2;

only b=0,1 remain. Local finiteness in ordinary degree justifies the
regrouping. It exploits an ALREADY KNOWN triangular factor; the Keller
identity alone has not supplied an analogous factor or regrouping.
No general inverse-degree or cancellation theorem is claimed.

The deformation distinction is equally literal:

    F_t=z-tH,  JF_t=1+4t(1-t)y(x+y^2).

DH is not nilpotent, despite JF_1=1. Zhao Lemma4.1 and Propositions4.2--4.5
retain nilpotence and polynomial inversion of the WHOLE t-deformation.
Theorem4.6 is an all-dimensions equivalence using homogeneous reduction,
not a plane-preserving reduction. Equation(3.11) also retains the factor
sum t^m A_m(q)=JG_t*q(G_t), not q(G_t) alone. These are primary-source
scope checks, not a refutation or repair of Zhao's formula.

The candidate was: on a normal AFFINE surface Y containing a marked WHOLE
U=A2_(x,y), dx wedge dy cannot have poles on Y-U (or at least cannot have
poles of order>=3). This would have been useful after removing an ample
dicritical divisor from a hypothetical projective Keller normalization,

Here is one exact counterexample, verified independently by ROOT and Astra.
Inside R=C[x,y], set

    a=x^4*y,
    c_i=x^(4-i)*y*(a-1)^i,  1<=i<=4,
    B=C[x,a,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4],  Y=Spec(B).

In the common fraction field set w=(a-1)/x. Then a=1+xw and c_i=a*w^i.
The complete chart identities are

    B_a     = C[x,w,(1+xw)^(-1)],
    B_(a-1) = C[x,y,(x^4*y-1)^(-1)],
    B_x     = C[x,x^(-1),y].

For the first use w=c_1/a; for the second use y=c_4/(a-1)^4.
D(a),D(a-1) cover Y, so it is smooth and hence normal. The morphism
induced by B subset R identifies the WHOLE source plane with
D_Y(x) union D_Y(a-1): their source opens cover because a-1=-1 when x=0.
No source curve is contracted or removed. The complement is
E=V_Y(x,a-1), entirely inside D(a); there E is x=0 with free coordinate w.
Thus E is one A1. At its generic point,

    y=x^(-4)+x^(-3)*w,
    dx wedge dy=x^(-3)*dx wedge dw,

so the volume has EXACT order-3 on E. This refutes the proposed implication,
not JC2. In fact a regular pair on Y cannot have nonzero constant source
Jacobian, since its differential wedge would be regular on E. No claim
about a finite Keller presentation or extra compactification hypotheses.
Do not enlarge the example into a family or assign a replacement control.

Keep an ACTUAL full-plane Keller pair F=(f,g) and an intermediate field with
d1=[C(x,y):K]=2. Let tau be its nontrivial deck involution, Gamma the finite
affine normalization of the target in C(x,y), and U=A2 its source open.
The old construction gives V=U union tau(U). Let W be the maximal etale
locus of Gamma->A2. By the ALREADY imported Stacks0ECD theorem, W is affine
as an open in affine Gamma. It is smooth and tau-invariant. It is tau-free:
at a fixed point local invertibility of the target map would make tau the
identity germ, hence the identity rational transformation.

Let D be the union of the divisorial components of W minus V. Since W is
smooth, its reduced divisor D is effective Cartier; its open complement
Gamma0 is affine (the inclusion is affine locally on W). Thus

    V = Gamma0 minus Z,  Z finite and tau-invariant,
    Gamma0 smooth affine, Gamma0->A2 etale, tau free on Gamma0.

No Mondal rational-singularity or Q-factoriality premise is needed. The
map Gamma0->A2 is NOT established finite. ROOT's preliminary concern that
purity required properness was incorrect: Stacks0BMB explicitly permits
quasi-finite maps with normal source, regular target, equal local dimensions,
and unramified codimension-one generizations. The direct common-divisor
removal argument also establishes etaleness, not the absence of holes.

Normality/Hartogs gives O(V)=O(Gamma0). Hence V is affine IFF Z is empty:
if both are affine their open inclusion induces an isomorphism of rings,
and therefore is an isomorphism. Freeness makes |Z| even, not necessarily0.
Localization and the vanishing of H3,H4 of a smooth affine complex surface
give H3(V,Q)=Q[Z], equivariantly for tau. Mayer--Vietoris gives the SAME
group as H2(U intersection tau(U),Q), with a minus sign from swapping the
two charts. This agrees with the retained nonvanishing possibility in

also gives H_c^1(Gamma0 minus U,Q)=0, but does not exclude its finite
intersection with the DIFFERENT boundary Gamma0 minus tau(U).

For an ACTUAL Keller pair use A=C[P,Q], R=C[x,y], K=Frac(A), L=Frac(R),
S=C[[u,v]] at an ordinary target node, k=Frac(S), T=R tensor_A S.
The map S->T is etale of finite presentation, so T is Noetherian normal.
It is a finite product of normal domains T_i. Each nonzero factor is
S-flat and dominates S; localizing by S minus zero gives a nonzero
finite-dimensional domain over k, hence its fraction field. Therefore

    Q(T) = T tensor_S k = L tensor_K k = product_i Frac(T_i).

Every idempotent eps of this EXACT generic algebra lies in T: it is
integral by eps^2-eps=0 and T is integrally closed in Q(T). This needs
no adic completion of T and no arbitrary polynomial idempotent of R.
It does NOT descend a splitting that exists only after a further field
extension of k. It also does NOT imply uv is a unit in eps*T. For example
S[1/u] is normal with generic field k and idempotent1, but v is not a unit.
Only with the additional unit premise does eps/(uv) belong to T and
yield the accepted forbidden trace n_i/(uv).

New scoped primary lead: Goodearl--Zhang, Poisson fields of two variables,
https://arxiv.org/html/2605.24835v1 . Read introduction, valuation definitions,
Lemma3.14/proof and selected family statements, not the whole paper or its
dependencies. Positive Dixmier-property cases do not include the Weyl field.
The valuation-height lemmas give height minus-infinity for Poisson subfields
of the Weyl field, not flag height zero. No actual intermediate field is
shown to enter an excluded family. This is an applicability screen, not a
new classification theorem. Scoped APP/notes/AUDIT searches found no named
entry for this paper; no exhaustive novelty claim.

ROOT's attempted bridge was to change the bracket, not merely rename field
coordinates. Let F=(p,q), JF=1, R=C[x,y], and phi=F^*. For nonzero rational h,
set {a,b}_h=h*J(a,b). The SAME phi preserves this bracket iff

    h(p,q)=h(x,y),

as testing x,y already shows. Constant h leaves the Weyl field. A useful
nonconstant h is missing; the original Jacobian identity does not supply it.

Manual full-source attachment: write a fixed rational h=a/b in lowest terms.
The polynomials a(F),b(F) are coprime: a common divisor would give a source
curve mapping into the finite common-zero set of a,b, contradicting
quasi-finiteness. From a(F)b=a b(F) and unique factorization, therefore,
a(F)=c*a and b(F)=c*b with c in C*. At least one is nonconstant, and each
belongs to every phi^k(R), since phi^k(a)=c^k*a and similarly for b.

Thus the proposed gauge already reaches the classical stable-image endpoint,
rather than evading it. Shpilrain--Yu math/9701210v1 Theorem1.6 states that a
nonautomorphic Keller map has intersection_k phi^k(R)=C; the related fixed-
polynomial result is Corollary1.7. The primary parsed423-line paper was read
whole. Its degree-comparison proof is not imported as an independently
checked argument here. The later author-hosted testpol.pdf was also read
whole360lines and explicitly invokes Kraft for the Keller case. Kraft's
institutional landing page timed out twice; his original proof was NOT read.
Accordingly the conclusion using that theorem is an external conditional
attachment, not a new promoted theorem or a claimed full dependency audit.

## 2026-09-14 14:57 UTC -- exact Liouville curve discriminator

Previous goal turn: bounded source-screening PROGRESS, not a closed JC2 gap.
This continuation selected and decided one new all-degree discriminator.
For an actual Keller pair, dS=x dy-f dg makes x dy exact on every f=c.
Would smoothness, closed plane embedding and regular exactness alone force
rationality? NO. ROOT's explicit p_n=x^2+x^(3n+2)y^n, odd n>=3, has for
every c!=0 a smooth closed irreducible fiber of genus(n-1)/2. Put t=x^3y,
v=1/x: its coordinate ring is exactly
C[t,v,v^-1]/(c*v^2-1-t^n), inverse x=1/v,y=t*v^3. Then

  x dy=d([t+(3n+2)*t^(n+1)/(2(n+1))]/c).

Thus even all generic fibers can be exact with unbounded genus. At n=3,c=1
the curve is x^2+x^11y^3=1 and the primitive t+11t^4/8. The WHOLE plane
pencil is critical on x=0 in its zero fiber; its parameter-dependent
primitive has a pole at c=0. No polynomial Keller mate is possible for this
p_n, directly from that critical line, without an accepted-bound audit.
This does not refute any accepted genus theorem or the actual-source
global-potential implication. The unpromoted curve-only proposal is stopped.

One bounded native Astra task instead checked a proposed quantum
exclusion route's FIRST existence premise. Let O=C[[h]], let A be a
finitely generated commutative complex Poisson algebra, and let A_h be
a unital O-flat deformation with [a_tilde,b_tilde]/h mod h={a,b}.
If A_h acts on a nonzero finite free O-module L, every point supporting
L/hL must be a zero of the Poisson tensor. Elementary proof:

- Matrix trace of the commutator vanishes. Cancelling h BEFORE reducing
  gives tau({a,b})=0, where tau(a)=Tr(a on L/hL).
- A composition series of the finite-dimensional commutative A-module
  L/hL gives tau(a)=sum_z n_z*a(z), n_z positive integers. Semisimplicity
  is NOT assumed; all nilpotent parts are retained via their lengths.
- For one support point z, Chinese remainders choose e=1 mod m_z^2,
  e=0 mod m_w^2 at all other support points. Leibniz gives
  {ea,eb}(z)={a,b}(z), zero at the other points. Hence
  n_z*{a,b}(z)=0 for ALL a,b. Characteristic zero gives the assertion.

Smooth symplectic S has no such zero, so that representation cannot
exist independently of any proposed regular Poisson pair. No exact-volume
or HP0=0 premise is needed. As the decisive control, the ordinary
symplectic plane also has no such representation yet has the pair(x,y).
Thus representation nonexistence supplies NO S/T scalar-pair exclusion.
An h-torsion skyscraper module is outside the finite-free hypothesis;
cancelling h on its endomorphisms would be invalid.

ROOT adds the elementary continuous-Laurent extension: a continuous
rho:A_h[h^-1]->Mat_r(C((h))) has rho(A_h) contained in h^-k Mat_r(O)
for some k>=0. The O-span of rho(A_h)O^r lies between O^r and h^-kO^r,
so is finite free, full rank and stable. The preceding argument applies.
This bounded-image meaning of continuity is explicitly the one following
Etingof--Schedler Theorem3.4, *Poisson traces, D-modules, and symplectic
resolutions*, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11005-017-1024-1 .

## 2026-09-14 19:46 UTC — the formal two-chart mate is already algebraic

Tick began19:37:08 on05f0e6cc88ffd23e3f9a264bbc44965aa83c0807.
ROOT revisited the existing formal construction before asking an
algebraization theorem to produce a global regular pair. ROOT and one
bounded native Astra task read WHOLE
xmodel/danielewski-two-chart-discriminator-astra-20260911.md,
full82d8c0b9b4ffe984791b2bbe9b6c9798ecd9dc5530a06ae68cded9b852d21ec0.
Its two plane charts, fixed-H=x obstruction and compatible formal mate
are already known; the following is a scope refinement, not a new route.

Let R=C[x,t,Z]/(t^2-1-x^2Z), T=SpecR, and set

    E=R[g]/(x^2*g^2-2*t*g+Z),       s=x^2*g-t.

Eliminating Z=2*t*g-x^2*g^2 turns the remaining defining equation
into (t-x^2*g)^2-1=0. Thus, WITHOUT cancelling x^2,

    E=C[x,g,s]/(s^2-1)=C[x,g] x C[x,g].

The s=-1 component has t=1+x^2*g, Z=2*g+x^2*g^2; it is exactly
the known chart T minus D_-. Its inverse is (t-1)/x^2 on D(x),
and Z/(t+1) on D(t+1); these open subsets cover that chart, including
D_+. The s=+1 component similarly has t=-1+x^2*g, Z=-2*g+x^2*g^2,
with inverses (t+1)/x^2 and Z/(t-1), and image T minus D_+.
Here D_+/- denotes x=0,t=+/-1. Both components are open immersions;
their disjoint union is surjective etale, NOT finite. For example, a
closed component has a proper dense open image, incompatible with a
finite map. Also the derivative in g is2*s, a unit.

The banked formal limit G_hat equals the two chart coordinates in their
x-adic completions. It therefore satisfies the displayed quadratic.
Its s_hat is -1 near D_+ and +1 near D_-: completion along x=0 is
disconnected and allows this choice. Completing this cover along x=0
recovers the same formal scheme. This is an exact algebraic realization
on an etale cover, not a regular function on the original connected T.

An R-section would force s=+1 or s=-1 everywhere because R is a domain.
The resulting rational roots (t+1)/x^2 and (t-1)/x^2 fail on D_+ and
D_- respectively: reduction of x^2*g=t+/-1 there gives0=+/-2.
Over K=FracR, E tensor_R K=K x K; the quadratic already splits into
these two rational roots. There is no quadratic FIELD extension, and
choosing a root in a field extension cannot realize the mixed formal
choice. The stronger no-mate claim for H=x remains the OLD transition
proof y+a(x)=v+b(x), v=y+2/x^2. Arbitrary H is still unrestricted.

Let A=C[p,q] subset S subset R=C[x,y], with S the finite normalization in
Frac R, and let h define its REDUCED BRANCH divisor B. Then

    {delta in Der_C(A): delta_tilde(S) subset S}
      = {delta: delta(h) in h*A}.

This is classical: Kallstrom, arXiv:math/0604559v3, Theorem2.2.1(L2--L3),
https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0604559v3 . Finiteness gives residual algebraicity;
normality and characteristic zero give the Krull/tame hypotheses. ROOT read
the introduction, theorem/proof and selected equal-characteristic local proof,
not the whole paper. Version July21,2007; internal PDF date November2,2018.
Locally h_i=c*z^e, e>1: regularity implies valuation(delta(h_i))>=e-1;
the base-field valuation is a multiple of e, hence >=e. The converse uses
tame lifting and the height-one intersection. Index-one omitted components
do not impose this condition; B must NOT be replaced by nonproperness D.

ROOT/Astra's direct source test: for two logarithmic fields with coefficient
rows (a_i,b_i), their determinant is in h*A, by tangency at each generic
branch point. Their inverse-Jacobian lifts consequently wedge into
h(p,q)*R*(partial_x wedge partial_y). For nonconstant h this does NOT span
the ordinary source tangent frame along h(p,q)=0, even using R-coefficients.
Moreover arbitrary R-coefficients need not extend across the normalization
boundary. Target coordinate changes transport the SAME intrinsic module;
they add no transverse partial. Thus the proposed strengthening stops, not
all derivation methods. No source-forced extra containment or new FIRST.

Candidate: set t=y^2-x^3 and let F_m=(U,V) be multiplication by m on the
generic elliptic curve Y^2=X^3+t over C(t), evaluated at (x,y), m>=3.
This gives rational functions, not a polynomial counterexample. It has
V^2-U^3=t, function-field degree m^2 and rational Jacobian m. Indeed the
relative invariant differential pulls back by m; wedging with dt gives

    dt wedge dx/(2y) = -dx wedge dy,
    dU wedge dV = m*dx wedge dy.

The differential equality before wedging is relative, modulo dt, not an
unjustified identity of absolute one-forms. Scaling (x,y,t) by weights
(2,3,6) preserves the zero section and commutes with multiplication, so U,V
are rational homogeneous of weights2,3. ROOT checked degree against Milne,
Elliptic Curves, II6.1, and the differential against III3.9--3.11:
https://jmilne.org/math/Books/EC2.pdf . These selected statements, not the
whole book/foundations, were read. No Galois assertion or total-degree
bound is used; m^2 is mapping degree. Identity m=1 is the positive control.

The decisive obstruction is the SAME finite normalization, not poles in a
particular coordinate formula. Put A=C[U,V], L=C(x,y), and S=the integral
closure of A in L. Here A need NOT lie in the original C[x,y]. With
T=y/x and w=y^2/x^3, L=C(w)(T), x=T^2/w,y=T^3/w, and
U=a(w)T^2,V=b(w)T^3. Since C(w)[T] is normal and contains A, it contains S.
Scaling preserves S; Vandermonde extraction retains each homogeneous
component. Thus S is positively graded, and evaluating a monic equation
at T=0 proves S_0=C. It is finite over A, Frac(S)=L, and its degree-zero
function field is C(w), so Proj(S)=P1.

Demazure--Watanabe now gives GLOBAL finite Cl(S), not merely local
Q-factoriality: Z -> Cl(P1)=Z maps1 to [ell*D] of positive degree, and the
remaining quotient is finite. ROOT read Singh--Spiroff arXiv0901.0686v1,
section2, Theorems2.1--2.2 and its explicit P1 consequence/Remark2.3:
https://arxiv.org/pdf/0901.0686v1 . Native Astra read the corresponding
author-hosted source. Original Watanabe publisher retrieval and ROOT's
author-hosted/PDF-screenshot attempts failed; no original-proof audit is

The following is MANUAL/UNPROMOTED stopping rationale, not a new theorem
packet or a different-model FIRST.

Literal conditional hypotheses: an actual polynomial Keller pair(p,q)
with ALL p-fibers irreducible. This is an assumption here; no Kaliman
reduction is imported or reverified. Remove finitely many atypical values
to obtain a smooth marked fibration over B. For a generic fiber C with
compactification Cbar and punctures P, put G=pi1(B) and
W=Q[P]/Q(sum of punctures), the peripheral submodule of H1(C,Q).
When finite-q and q-pole punctures are both nonempty, their two invariant
types give a nonzero invariant residue functional lambda in(W dual)^G.
Writing their cardinalities r,s, respectively, its weights are s on the
finite-q punctures and -r on the poles. This statement keeps the explicit
nonempty-type hypothesis; puncture counts are not assumed for every fiber.

The source complement gives H1-cohomology invariants H^1(C,Q)^G=0:
H^1(p^-1(B),Q) is generated by meridians of the removed irreducible,
reduced fibers, p*:H^1(B,Q)->H^1(p^-1(B),Q) is an isomorphism, and the
Leray edge sequence has H^2(B,Q)=0. Invariant peripheral HOMOLOGY is
not invariant whole-fiber COHOMOLOGY. The exact obstruction is the
G-module extension

  0 -> H^1(Cbar,Q) -> H^1(C,Q) -> W dual -> 0.

For any linear lift lambda_tilde, the compact-period cocycle
c_g=g(lambda_tilde)-lambda_tilde represents the connecting class.
H^1(C,Q)^G=0 makes that connecting map injective: the displayed nonzero
lambda cannot lift invariantly. A Keller-mate argument would have to force
this same class to vanish. Neither pure compact-fiber semisimplicity nor
the existence of puncture orbits supplies a splitting of this extension.

The direct actual-source tests do not do so. The etale image of F is open
and has no omitted divisor: otherwise h(F) would be a nonconstant unit in
C[x,y]. Its complement is therefore finite, and q:C->A1 is surjective
after avoiding the finitely many corresponding p-values. Choose finite T
so q is finite etale over A1 minus T. Each target meridian has an unramified
interior preimage whose small loop dies when the deleted interior points
are filled back into C. Thus a target character pulled back by q can
descend to H1(C) only if it is zero. Equivalently, a rational target
differential whose pullback is regular on C has no finite poles, so is
P(q)dq and exact. This does not exclude sheet-dependent corrections.

For K=C(p), unique factorization and the irreducible reduced p-a fibers
also give (C[x,y] tensor_C[p] K)^*=K^*. Global generic-fiber dlog-unit
corrections therefore vanish on a fiber. This does NOT exclude units
after finite/algebraic base extension, norm-one phenomena, or units on an
individual fiber. Finally dH=xdy-pdq restricts to
xdy=d(H+cq) on p=c, already exact; it gives no nonzero residue functional.

Take ANY f,g in C[x,y] with J(f,g)=1, and write A=C[f,g]. The injective
polynomial-ring substitutions

  phi1: (x,y) -> (t^2/2,s),
  phi2: (x,y) -> (s,-t^2/2)

both have Jacobian t. Hence both pulled-back pairs have Jacobian t and
are even in t. If the proposed integrality assertion held for them, then
t^2/2=phi1(x) and -t^2/2=phi2(y) would be integral over phi1(A) and
phi2(A), respectively. Pulling the monic equations back through the
injective maps proves that BOTH x and y are integral over A. Consequently
C[x,y] is finite over A. The original Keller map is then finite etale,
so a connected finite covering of simply connected C^2, and is an
automorphism. A single selected-coordinate integrality claim was NOT
used as sufficient: the TWO substitutions are essential to this argument.

substitution give J(f,g)=1. Automorphy gives t^2/2 in C[P,Q], so t
satisfies a monic quadratic over that algebra. Thus the universal
assertion restricted to EVEN-IN-t pairs is JC2-equivalent. The assertion
for arbitrary linear-Jacobian pairs IMPLIES JC2; no converse for that
unrestricted assertion is established. This is an implication/equivalence

## 2026-09-15 00:45 UTC — fixed Long base has only one locally nilpotent Hamiltonian direction

canonical fixed-pair and tangent-coordinate stops. No donor-family scan

ROOT read Long's opening, bracket convention and Section3 definitions
through the opening of H, not the whole paper this tick. In source
coordinates (x,q,p,z), put

  a=1-3xq, beta=3x^2*p+2a*z-9q^2, y=q-x*beta/3, u=xy,
  R=x(2-3xq),
  T=-((1+u)^3*beta+y^2*(1+u)*(4+3u))/2,
  {f,g}=f_p*g_x-f_x*g_p+f_z*g_q-f_q*g_z, delta_H={H,-}.

These are the fixed formulas of [Long v1, Sections2-3](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.23777v1).
The source attachment is not a promotion of its ambient claims. ROOT's
bounded gate and native Astra corroboration give, for EVERY H(U,V) in C[U,V],

  delta_(H(R,T)) is locally nilpotent iff H belongs to C[U].

Proof: delta_R=-(2-6xq)*partial_p+3x^2*partial_z is locally nilpotent:
it fixes its coefficients and lowers degree in p,z. Direct substitution
gives delta_R(beta)=delta_R(y)=0, hence {R,T}=0. At (1,0,0,0),
beta=y=0, beta_p=3, y_p=-1, and T_p=-3/2. Thus delta_T(x) is
nonzero. Also dR=2dx-3dq there while dT has nonzero dp coefficient,
so R,T are algebraically independent; no ambient symplectic audit is needed.

If delta_(H(R,T)) is locally nilpotent, its invariant R=x(2-3xq)
forces x invariant by factorial closure of an LND kernel. For completeness,
in a characteristic-zero domain the top Leibniz term gives
deg_delta(fg)=deg_delta(f)+deg_delta(g); an invariant product therefore
has invariant factors. The chain rule now gives

  0=delta_(H(R,T))(x)=H_V(R,T)*delta_T(x).

The domain property and algebraic independence give H_V=0, hence H in C[U].
Conversely delta_(h(R))=h'(R)*delta_R is LND because its multiplier is
in ker(delta_R). This includes constants. Controls: H=U succeeds and
H=V fails. In particular NO algebraically independent pair in C[R,T]
has both Hamiltonians LND; polynomial base reparameterization cannot fix
the proposed simultaneous-LND reduction. Hamiltonians involving D,S are
OUTSIDE this conclusion. The putative common-kernel polynomial-plane
quotient was conditional, not established or needed for this failed gate.

Put u=x^2*y, p=x+x^5*y^2=x(1+u^2), and

The time coordinate q is RATIONAL, with genuine poles at u=+/-i;
it is not a polynomial Keller mate. The polynomial p is a submersion:
p_x=1+5u^2 and p_y=2x^3*u never vanish together. Thus
delta_p=-2x^5*y*partial_x+(1+5x^4*y^2)*partial_y is nonzero everywhere
and divergence-free. Directly {p,u}=xp and {p,q}=1.

omitted, with critical values b_+/-(c)=+/-2i/(3c^2). Off those values

avoiding them therefore lifts for ALL real time. The exceptional initial
points form a measure-zero set: (p,u) are global coordinates on p!=0,
the fiberwise exceptional level sets have real area zero, and Fubini

### Separate Laurent-polynomial donor dichotomy: retained proof DRAFT

ROOT proposed the following algebraic filter during the constructive pass.
Astra hand-checked it in one bounded message-only task and independently
observed COMPLETED at intake. Same producing model: NOT different-model
FIRST. Status MANUAL/DRAFT/UNPROMOTED, not a new accepted campaign closure.
History/primary-premise reconciliation is incomplete; no novelty claim.

Let p,u be independent and, for m>=2 and any integer k, put

  q=P(p,u)=p^(-k)*u^m + sum_(0<=j<m) a_j(p)*u^j,
  a_j in C[p,p^(-1)], A=C[p,q], K=C(p,u).

Let S be the normalization of A in K. The second-leg field degree is m.
Over p!=0, S[p^(-1)]=C[p,p^(-1),u], since the leading coefficient is
a unit there. This is an actual finite normal cover, ramified on P_u=0.
The proposed dichotomy is:

1. A critical-value Puiseux branch over p=0 has a pole. Its actual branch
   image has an infinity place with p tending to0 and q tending to infinity.
   Its normalization is not A1: the nonconstant p would be a polynomial
   on A1 and could not remain finite at its unique infinity place.
2. Every critical-value Puiseux branch over p=0 is integral. Then
   S=C[t,v]^(mu_m) for the diagonal action described below; in particular
   m*Cl(S)=0. The quantifier EVERY branch is essential.

Here is the retained manual proof of case2. Center u using
s(p)=-p^k*a_(m-1)(p)/m, set p=t^m and u=s(t^m)+t^k*v. Then

  H(t,v)=P(t^m,s(t^m)+t^k*v)
        =v^m + sum_(0<=j<=m-2) c_j(t)*v^j,
  c_j in C[t,t^(-1)].

This works for negative k as well. Critical values are unchanged by the
affine source change and are integral by hypothesis. If some c_j has a
pole, let r=max_j(-ord_t(c_j)/(m-j))>0, omitting zero coefficients.
After a finite ramified extension, G(w)=t^(mr)*H(t,t^(-r)*w) is integral,
monic and centered, and its reduction has a nonzero lower coefficient.
Every critical value of this reduced polynomial is zero: roots of G'
are integral and lift its reduced roots, counted with multiplicity, and
their G-values equal t^(mr) times integral critical values of H.

But a monic centered characteristic-zero polynomial all of whose
critical values vanish is w^m. Indeed if it has s distinct roots, its
derivative has exactly m-s zeros counted with multiplicity at those roots;
all m-1 derivative zeros being there forces s=1, and centering puts that
root at0. This contradicts the retained nonzero lower coefficient.
Thus each c_j is integral and, being Laurent, belongs to C[t]. Repeated
critical roots do not require simple-root Hensel lifting; factoring over
an algebraic closure of the valued field suffices.

Now B=C[t,v] is finite over A by t^m=p and the monic relation H(t,v)=q.
It is normal with field C(t,v). The action

  (t,v) -> (zeta*t,zeta^(-k)*v), zeta^m=1,

fixes p,u,q. Since t^m-p is irreducible over C(p,u), its fixed field is
exactly K and S=B^(mu_m). The action is faithful on t even when k and m
are not coprime. Invariant-ring normality and finiteness identify the
global normalization, not just a local chart. Weil-divisor pullback to
the factorial B followed by norm gives m*Cl(S)=0.

Proposed interface with existing campaign criteria, to be source-pinned
before promotion: a dominant rational substitution into C(x,y) making
p,q polynomial Keller outputs gives A -> S -> R=C[x,y], because R is
normal and every element of S is integral over A. This is NOT assumed
birational and does NOT license an open-immersion argument. The accepted
arbitrary-first-leg compulsory-branch criterion would exclude case1:
the branch must be a nonproperness component, whose normalization is A1.
The accepted torsion-class criterion would exclude case2: effective
ramification has a principal positive multiple; its pullback cannot
vanish on the etale quasi-finite source and hence is a constant unit.
Dominance forces no ramification; purity and finite etale triviality of
A2 then force m=1, contrary to the donor degree. These interfaces are
consumed at their recorded scope, not newly promoted by this draft.

Controls and scope attacks retained:

- q=(u^3+u)/p^2 has critical values with poles at p=0, illustrating case1.
- q=u^m illustrates case2 with an affine-plane normalization, still ramified.
- q=u^2/p has S=C[p,q,u]/(u^2-pq), the mu_2 quotient of C[t,v]; this is
  only a closed-degree control, not a new frontier search.
- m=1 is deliberately excluded and admits polynomial automorphism examples.
- A pure-power special equation does NOT prove an irreducible normalized
  special fiber: u^2-p^2-p^3*q=0 normalizes to v^2-1=p*q with u=p*v.
  The quotient proof does not make that false inference.

The donor class excludes rational dependence with multiple poles in u,
leading coefficients having additional finite zeros/poles in p, and
arbitrary rulings not supplied by the target coordinate p. It is not a
